name: Westmoor County

location.about: An old county town of about 180,000 where the moors meet the Somerset levels: wool, then cider, then cars and insurance offices. One of the oldest clubs in the land - and the best cup side England has ever had.

colours.story: Sky blue and navy - the sky over the moor and the navy of the county regiment, whose officers helped found the club in 1869.

home.shirt: sky blue with a navy collar

rivals.why: the market town fifteen miles down the levels - the county's two clubs, at it since 1883
the 8-1 at Moorside Park in 1999 - still sung about on the Cider End

history.title: The county's club
history.text: Founded in 1869 by officers of the county regiment and the town's grammar school. In the Founders' Cup from its first year: beaten finalists in 1873 and 1875, winners in 1878, 1892 and 1897 - the year of the club's first title, the Double.

history.title: So near, then the long wait
history.text: Second three years running (1900, 1901, 1902), champions again in 1930 - and then thirty years with nothing, until the Founders' Cup final of 1962 was lost too.

history.title: Kings of the cup
history.text: Champions in 1963 - and relegated three years later. Back as Second Division champions in 1967, the same spring they won the Founders' Cup; won it again in 1968, the Charter Cup in 1969, and the Founders' Cup in 1971, 1972 and 1974. Down again, and up as champions in 1977.

history.title: Ups and downs
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1990, second in the league in 1994 - then relegation, and back up through the play-offs in 1997. In 1999 they won 8-1 against Eastvale.

history.title: The best of times
history.text: Champions in 2006 and again in 2009 - with the Founders' Cup, the club's second Double, 112 years after the first. The Founders' Cup in 2012 and 2019, the Charter Cup in 2014: twelve Founders' Cups, level with Bramhall for the most.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1897 = 1896-97).

legends.name: Colonel Edwin Rayne
legends.note: Officer of the county regiment; the Rayne Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Len Tapscott
legends.note: Six cups in nine years; the Second Division title in 1967 and 1977.

legends.name: Matt Corrigan
legends.note: Lifted both titles and the 2009 Double.

legends.name: Joel Hartnell
legends.note: Scored in the 2019 Founders' Cup final.

records.attendance: 61,034 v Holloway Vale, Founders' Cup fifth round, 1972 (Moorside Park, before seating)

badge.about: The moor's tor and the county's stag; the twelve stars round the edge for the twelve Founders' Cups. Motto 'Semper Fidelis' - always faithful, the county regiment's.
badge.design: A sky-blue circle with a navy ring around it. In the centre a navy stag standing on a rocky hilltop (a tor). 'WESTMOOR COUNTY' in sky blue capitals around the navy ring, with '1869' at the bottom. Twelve small amber stars spaced around the outside of the ring.

ground.name: Moorside Park

stands.name: Rayne Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts, the trophy room with twelve Founders' Cup replicas

stands.name: Cider End
stands.features: the home end - one steep single tier in sky blue, named after the cider works that stood behind it

stands.name: Moor Stand
stands.features: two tiers with the moor rising behind them - the view from the top row is famous

stands.name: Levels End
stands.features: away fans; low and old - the club's next rebuild

ground.surroundings: the moor rising green and brown behind the east stand, the old cider works' chimney, the cathedral-sized church of the market square, apple orchards on the edge of town
ground.atmosphere: proud and old-fashioned - and on cup days the loudest ground in the South West
